name: Plapo Krumen
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: The Krumen languages are tone languages, like many other languages in all the continents of the world. The words differ not only by consonants and vowels, but also by tones (like piches in music). In the Atlas Linguistique Kru (1983:148), Marchese notes that all Kru languages studied have either four or three tone levels. The Krumen cluster – Tepo, Plapo and Piè – fits the general picture of the Kru languages: All three languages are characterized by a three-level tone system – high / mid / low [...] Each syllable of a given word is a potential tone bearing unit TBU; e.g. the vowel « a » is a carrier of one of the four level tones: H (á), M (ā), La (à) and Lb (à).
new_statements.citation: Thalmann, Peter. 2026. Tonal puzzles in 3 Krumen languages (SW of Côte d'Ivoire): phonological, grammatical and historical issues. Ms., 3rd revised version (1st 2018, 2nd 2020), SIL; 40 pp. https://kroumen.com/sites/www.kroumen.com/files/pdf-files/2026%20Krumen%20Tones%20ver3%
new_statements.locator: section 2.1 'Tone inventory: four tonemes (H, M, La, Lb) on three levels', p. 6 (see also sec. 1.4 p. 4)
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences

new_statements.rule_in_words: Plapo Krumen (with Tepo and Piè) is described as a tone language with three tone levels and four tonemes (H, M, two low tones La/Lb, plus a LbH rising sequence), every syllable being a tone-bearing unit; the author says nothing about word stress or accent, and none of the Krumen descriptions consulted (1980 phonology, 1987/2023 Tepo grammar, 1993 Plapo primer) contains a stress statement.
new_statements.exceptions: none regarding stress; the Tepo grammar (Thalmann 2023: 14) mentions 'un phénomène d'accentuation' only as an explanation for tonal pre-association in a handful of lexemes, without defining stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern lexical tone on syllables of words; no word- or phrase-level stress domain is discussed. Source treats Plapo directly (Plapo consultant Toto Nemlin Laurent), alongside Tepo and Piè.
new_statements.identity_note: The only Plapo-direct sources are Thalmann's 2018/2020/2026 tone paper (Tepo [ted], Plapo [ktj], Piè [pye] treated side by side) and the 1993 SIL Plapo syllabary ('plaapo, baipo, hompo'). The fuller descriptions (Thalmann 1980 Phonologie du kroumen; 1987/2023 Eléments de grammaire kroumen tépo) describe Tepo Krumen (tepo1239, Grabo variety), which the 1980 dialect survey groups with Plapo at ~100% intercomprehension; note the 2023 grammar's title page misprints the code as [ktj] though the text says [ted]. Thoiré 1933 'plaoui' = Plapo and Babo of the Tabou river basin (data from 1901).

sources.citation: Thalmann, Peter. 2023 [1987]. Eléments de grammaire kroumen tépo (parler kru de Côte d'Ivoire). Revised re-edition (file '230801 Grammaire kroumen [ted]', 492 pp.) of the 1987 thèse de doctorat, Université Paris 7. Tepo Krumen (tepo1239), Grabo variety; tone chapter revised with Plapo, Piè and Grebo data.
sources.note: Ch. 0 'Introduction phonologique' pp. 9-60 (phonemes, nasalisation, 0.3 Les tons pp. 17-26: 'langue à trois niveaux tonals' H, M, Ba, Bb + BH; syllable; phonological word; tone distribution). No section or sentence on word stress; only 0.1.4 p. 14 invokes 'un phénomène d'accentuation' to explain tonal pre-association in a few lexemes (tùpǎ, tǔgbà).
